boundary: External build prerequisites with a pinned, reproducible identity. Each entry records where the bytes come from, how they are built or unpacked, and the exact identities the build gate re-verifies. A local cache may satisfy an entry, but a cache is never the only source: every entry stays obtainable from the recorded upstream input plus the recipe below, so an empty working set can be rebuilt without any diagnostic directory.

tree-sitter.required_because: xtask/src/treesit.rs rejects any other SDK before a compiler starts; the 0.27.1 header fixes TSInput.decode and the struct layout the mirror was written against.

steps: download the pinned upstream tarball and verify sha256
extract into an owner-chosen prefix; the tree-sitter top directory becomes the build root
verify the identities in `identities` below against the installed prefix
recipe.notes: AMALGAMATED=1 is what the pinned Homebrew formula used; it produces the single-header amalgamation this project's mirror was captured from. The pkg-config file must describe the actual chosen prefix, not a fixed absolute path.

tree-sitter.supported_hosts: Apple Silicon macOS; this pin says nothing about other hosts or older systems
tree-sitter.identities_note: Only the header identity is a hard build constraint: xtask/src/treesit.rs checks that digest and the pkg-config version, then links whatever dylib the prefix provides. The dylib bytes legitimately differ between a Homebrew bottle and a source build of the same 0.27.1 tree (compiler and layout choices), so a dylib byte pin would reject a correct rebuild. For reference only, the bottle used earlier had lib/libtree-sitter.dylib fb5a5dcc685b7b541f25d87a3028928e900d60a96da809f206d69fd3a4fe3d78, while a source build from the pinned tarball produces a different but equally valid library.
